sections.heading: A CONVERSATION WITH KOTARO ISAKA?
sections.content:
Q: Do you have any contact with Kotaro Isaka-sensei? Any chance of a joint interview?

A: That'd be like asking a rookie manga artist to sit down for a talk with Takehiko Inoue — completely impossible…[ref:isaka-inoue]

sections.heading: PLANNING CHARACTER CONNECTIONS
sections.content:
Q: I really love the relationships between characters across your different works — was that all mapped out from the very beginning?

A: No, it gets tacked on after the fact, crunch by crunch.[ref:donbei-slogan]

sections.heading: DON'T LET THE COMPETITION DISCOURAGE YOU
sections.content:
Q: I also entered the Dengeki Novel Award, and it's brutally hard to advance — I've been struggling. Just seeing how many people submitted made me feel a kind of despair. And then I realized that professional writers, Iruma-sensei included, must all just be geniuses, and now I want to give up. Please give me some advice, and some encouragement to reignite the fire.

A: There's no such thing as "I couldn't score a 90 because there were so many other people around." No matter how many people enter, your own score reflects your own ability. Don't worry about the number of entrants — just write it, and submit it with confidence.

sections.heading: WHAT IT TAKES TO WRITE
sections.content:
Q: What's essential when writing a novel?

A: Believing you have talent. And stubborn, unshakable grit.

sections.heading: MORE NAGOYA, PLEASE
sections.content:
Q: Iruma-sensei, please put more Nagoya flavor into your work.

A: Go read Six Guns, Six People, Six Days! Please, read it… please…

sections.heading: WILL YOU BE MY FRIEND?
sections.content:
Q: Iruma-sensei, here's my question: will you please be my friend?

A: Is that a question…? I mean, sure, I guess.

sections.heading: YAMANA'S FAMILY, AND ANOTHER RECRUIT
sections.content:
Q: I love Iruma Hitoma-sensei the most! I'm still just a hobbyist, but I write novels too. Please, let me join the Iruma Legion! Also, I love Liar, Broken, and I'm really curious about the story of Big Sister Yamana's family — do you have any plans to write something with her as the lead?

A: Probably not (I couldn't remember who Big Sister Yamana was for a second there — let's keep that between us).

sections.heading: FINDING YOUR OWN GENRE
sections.content:
Q: I also post novels on a certain writing site, but nobody ever leaves comments. Since I'm a talentless nobody, I suppose that's only to be expected. I'm honestly baffled by just how unsuited I am to writing. Setting that aside — I don't even know what genre I'm suited to. When did Iruma-sensei figure out which genre suited him?

A: Even now, I don't know which genre I'm suited to, because I've written all kinds of different things. But I don't think you need that kind of limitation to begin with. Write whatever you want to write.

sections.heading: STILL CAN'T FIND THE ISOLATED
sections.content:
Q: Iruma-sensei, Iruma-sensei — no matter how many bookstores I go to, I can't find The Isolated. Why?! Also, I really love My Small-Scale Miracle — is there really no sequel to that one?

A: The Isolated is scheduled for a print release next year, so please hold on until then… As for a sequel to Small-Scale, there almost certainly won't be one. In a certain sense, that book is already its own sequel, or epilogue.[ref:small-scale-origin]

sections.heading: WATCHING YOUR WORK GO MULTIMEDIA
sections.content:
Q: How does it feel for Iruma-sensei to see his work adapted across different media?

A: Incredibly happy. Though, before I knew it, the manga serialization had ended,[ref:denpa-manga-end] which was pretty sad.

sections.heading: A SAMURAI HAIRSTYLE?
sections.content:
Q: Iruma-sensei's formal wear is a yukata — so is his hairstyle a chonmage?

A: It's a samurai.

sections.heading: SPOKEN OR WRITTEN, AND ANOTHER RECRUIT
sections.content:
Q: So, after reading through the Q&A sessions, I found myself wondering: what actually is the difference between spoken and written language? They say "there's no shame in asking, only in not knowing," so here I am asking. Also, please let me join the Iruma Legion too! (dogeza)

A: I don't know either! An answer like that is probably what "spoken language" sounds like.

sections.heading: WHEN STORIES END TOO QUICKLY
sections.content:
Q: I'm writing a novel, but the story always either wraps up too fast or ends up feeling flat. Any advice?

A: Isn't wrapping up fast just fine, though? A long story isn't necessarily better than a short one. What matters most, ultimately, is what you actually want to write. Also, this kind of question is better suited for the Dengeki Bunko radio show.

sections.heading: LONG HAIR, SHORT HAIR, OR A SINGLE PONYTAIL
sections.content:
Q: Does Iruma-sensei prefer long hair or short hair on women? I like both long and short hair myself, but what I love most of all is a single ponytail. Ah, I also think the shaved-head Nakamura-san from The Isolated is pretty cute too, but that's an exception among exceptions. None of your works have a single-ponytail girl — will one show up eventually? Huh? Twin tails? Ha ha, what are you even talking about, that doesn't even come close to a single ponytail. What I'm trying to say is: Iruma, tie your hair into a single ponytail and marry me, and everything will be fine! That's all.

A: If I absolutely had to pick one, I prefer people with long hair.

sections.heading: HOW TO SPEND A FINAL FREE SUMMER
sections.content:
Q: I'm at a vocational school and due to graduate next year. Since I'll be spending the next year job hunting, I want to spend the rest of this year having as much fun as possible. Any recommendations?

A: How about the gym? Swimming in a pool is a lot of fun.

sections.heading: THE MARRIAGE LAW LOOPHOLE
sections.content:
Q: I finished Small-Scale! I loved both pairings — "I (ore) × her" and "I (watashi) × Handsome-maru." By the way, about that line Handsome-maru (Tomato) says — "suppose I marry your little sister, and you marry my little sister; would we then have to call each other 'brother'?" — if "I (ore)" marries "her," then Handsome-maru and "I (watashi)" both become "I (ore)'s" younger siblings, and Japanese civil law bans marriage between siblings, so Handsome-maru and "I (watashi)" wouldn't be able to marry each other after all.[ref:japan-marriage-law] And vice versa. …What should be done about this?

A: Whoever loses at rock-paper-scissors gives up on getting married…

sections.heading: A DRAGON'S CROWN DUEL?
sections.content:
Q: Iruma-sensei! I challenge you to a one-on-one battle in Dragon's Crown! Please accept!

A: I don't do online multiplayer, sorry. Because of that, I can't even do the Pokémon trade-evolution thing.

sections.heading: FLORA OVER LUDMAN
sections.content:
Q: Besides Ludman, who did you choose as your bride in Dragon Quest V?[ref:dq5-ludman-again]

A: I always go with Flora. Rather than yellow, I prefer blue.[ref:dq5-hair-color]

sections.heading: LATE BECAUSE OF YOU
sections.content:
Q: Because my thoughts about Iruma-sensei were just too strong, I ended up being late! Please help me!

A: Don't skip sleep at night! Sleep once you get where you're going! Please don't actually do that!

sections.heading: A SWEET TOOTH
sections.content:
Q: Yo, sensei. It's a pretty ordinary question, but — what food do you like?

A: I like pretty much anything sweet.

sections.heading: REAL PLACES IN FICTION
sections.content:
Q: Are there any scenes in Iruma-sensei's work drawn from real personal experience — like the view from your own house, for example?

A: Train stations and shopping centers are places I've actually walked through myself. Anyone who knows those places will probably recognize them the moment they read it.

sections.heading: NEXT MONTH FOR SIX GUNS
sections.content:
Q: Every single one of your works, I read with joy. I became your fan by starting with Liar, Broken, on a friend's recommendation. Anyway, question time: when does the sequel to Six Guns, Six People, Six Days come out? I want to read the continuation as soon as possible. Also, it'd be great if My Small-Scale Miracle got a sequel too.

A: Next month. And as I already mentioned, Small-Scale is already close to being its own sequel, so a further one probably isn't happening.

sections.heading: THE FASTEST TITLE EVER
sections.content:
Q: Iruma-sensei's titles are always so distinctive — which of your works took the longest to title, and which one came together the fastest? I'm not very good at coming up with titles myself, so I'm curious how other people do it.

A: The Naked Idiot Comes Running — that title took three seconds to decide.[ref:baka-zenra]

sections.heading: THE WORLD AT FOURTEEN
sections.content:
Q: How did Iruma-sensei see the world at age fourteen?

A: It looked incredibly narrow. Which is probably why I turned out to be such an idiot.

sections.heading: MORE ELECTRIC GIRL AND HANASAKI TAROU?
sections.content:
Q: I love Electric Girl and the Hanasaki Tarou series. Any plans for a sequel or short-story collection down the line?

A: If Electric Girl got a second anime season, I could probably write ten more volumes, ha ha ha. Also, there might be more Hanasaki Tarou next year (Note: there was not).

sections.heading: NOT A LOLICON
sections.content:
Q: Is Iruma-sensei a lolicon?

A: If anything, I'm bad with actual children — I have no idea what to even say to them.

sections.heading: MISSING THE SIGNING EVENTS
sections.content:
Q: I'd love to see more events! Any chance of a signing session?

A: Nobody invites me to signing events anymore… I'm so lonely.

sections.heading: GIVE ME A THEME
sections.content:
Q: I'm currently in the literature club and want to write a new novel, but I haven't settled on a theme… Iruma-sensei, could you give me one?

A: Well, if I could come up with a theme, I'd just write it myself! So I can't give you one, sorry.

sections.heading: IS THAT AKKYUN'S STAND-IN?
sections.content:
Q: Question: in the "Super Iruma War" story that crosses over Liar, Broken, Electric Girl, The Lizard King, and "The Sky Falls Because of Eyes" (File.03, "Mixer, Side B"), the dead-eyed young man — is that the stand-in Akkyun from Liar, Broken? That's Amano ×-kun, right?[ref:super-iruma-war]

A: Probably.

sections.heading: YUZU'S PEN NAME
sections.content:
Q: In the "Super Iruma War" story "Radio from Another Dimension," the pen name "Yuu-yuu" that shows up — that's Fushimi Yuzu, right? So the person she's confessing to has their ears plugged up… that's also ×-kun. Ah, this one's Yuzu too, right?

A: Most likely.

sections.heading: MORE CROSSOVER CONFIRMATIONS
sections.content:
Q: In the "Super Iruma War" story "Weekly Mofu News," the first witness — that's ×-kun after all, right?! Mayu shows up too! Also, in "Super Iruma War"'s "Mixer, Side B," the unhappy-looking girl next to the dead-eyed young man is ×-ne (Amano ×-ne), right? And the lady with the hair ornament is Geronimo (Uegoro Natsuki), right?

A: Definitely.

sections.heading: A FUTURE RIVAL ASKS FOR AN AUTOGRAPH
sections.content:
Q: Since I'll be debuting as a novelist in about two years, we'll be rivals by then. So, please give me your autograph.

A: I think I'll save that gift for when we meet after your debut. Good luck.

sections.heading: VOLUME 2, WITH A HANASAKI TAROU CAMEO
sections.content:
Q: I like Six Guns, Six People, Six Days partly because Hanasaki Tarou shows up in it, but is there really not going to be a second volume?

A: It's coming out next month. It even includes illustrations of Hanasaki Tarou and Kisogawa.

sections.heading: WILL THE NEW WORLD THEME SONG GET A CD?
sections.content:
Q: I bought New World! The theme song was so good that I wanted to recommend it to a friend, but will this song ever get a CD release?

A: Hmm — I wonder how that'll go. Will it get included on an album?[ref:new-world-song]

sections.heading: NAMING THE TWINS, AND A NICKNAME
sections.content:
Q: Would "Ayu" be a good name for ×-kun and Ma-chan's daughter? Also, can Iruma-sensei's nickname just be "Iruman"? Is that settled, then?

A: I'd actually already decided on a name for their daughter, but I've forgotten it, so sure, that works too. Also, my nickname can be whatever. Unrelated to any of this, but my name written in Roman letters is "hitomairuma" — I keep wondering whether that actually lets people tell my given name and surname apart.[ref:ayu-mai-twins]

sections.heading: THE EASIEST CHARACTER TO WRITE
sections.content:
Q: Among all the characters you've written so far, has there ever been one whose thoughts and actions you found hard to imagine, and who was difficult to write? If so, who was the hardest to write?

A: I can never really imagine any of my characters' thoughts or actions in the first place — which, conversely, means the easiest character for me to write is Fujiwa Jojo.

sections.heading: GUESSING THE SISTER'S NAME
sections.content:
Q: The half-sister of Akkyun — second-generation, also known as Amano ×-kun — from Liar, Broken, the one referred to as "Nimouto" — is her name Aine? Amano Aine, is that right?

A: Please don't ask me too many questions like this… it's embarrassing.

sections.heading: AN ALBUM FOR NIJOU OWARI?
sections.content:
Q: Please release an album for Nijou Owari! You have to! After hearing the Liar, Broken image album, I want one no matter what!

A: That'd be a little tough. She's not exactly the protagonist of the series, after all.

sections.heading: COULD ADACHI AND SHIMAMURA GET ANIMATED?
sections.content:
Q: I finished reading Adachi and Shimamura. Could this one make it onto broadcast TV?

A: That'll depend on how much support it gets from everyone… please keep cheering it on! Honestly, though, since there's so little action in it, I don't think it'd be all that interesting even as an anime.

sections.heading: WOULD YOU FETCH ME TEA?
sections.content:
Q: I finished The Thing Your Eyes Were Searching For — it's a book that made me reconfirm, "I really do love Iruma Hitoma the most!" Thank you for writing something so wonderful! By the way, after reading "Season of Static," I have a question. In that story, there's a line about how "some guys want to be gentle to girls, and some guys are too embarrassed to manage it." If I (16 years old, high schooler, chestnut hair, E-cup) asked Iruma-sensei to go buy me a Healthya green tea, would you be the type to run out and get it?[ref:healthya]

A: If you properly hand me the money for the tea, I'll go buy it. Though I don't actually like the taste of Healthya green tea.

sections.heading: FRIENDS, TAKE TWO
sections.content:
Q: This might be a rude question, but last time you said you didn't have any friends — so, can we be friends?

A: There's no real upside to being my friend, you know — if you're fine with that, then sure, I guess.

sections.heading: HOW TO WRITE A SUBMISSION SYNOPSIS
sections.content:
Q: Since I had some free time, I wrote a novel, and it's got enough pages, so I want to submit it to the Dengeki Award. But I don't really understand how to write the content synopsis you're supposed to attach. Should I write it like the blurb on a book's inside flap (or back cover, for MediaWorks), or should I go into detail all the way through to the ending? Please teach me, sensei!

A: Please write it in detail, all the way to the ending. Incidentally, questions like this should go to the Dengeki Bunko radio show, as previously mentioned, et cetera.

sections.heading: NO ROOM FOR DESPAIR
sections.content:
Q: When you feel hopeless about the future, what kind of things does Iruma-sensei imagine? How long do you want to live?

A: I've never had that kind of experience. No matter what happens, I always figure something will work out somehow.

sections.heading: A YEAR-LONG DIARY, AND A BIRTHDAY REQUEST
sections.content:
Q: I finished reading Akkyun and Ma-chan's diary,[ref:mikun-diary] but when will it get expanded into a full 365-day version? Also, is there any established setting for the two of their birthdays? If it hasn't been decided yet, how about setting Akkyun's birthday as June 27th?

A: I haven't thought through that level of detail, but sure, that date you suggested works fine. Though I have no idea what's significant about that day.

sections.heading: A RECOMMENDED READ
sections.content:
Q: Of all the books Iruma-sensei has read, which would you recommend the most?

A: Laozi's work, obviously! If manga counts too, the recent World Trigger is a lot of fun.

sections.heading: MEASUREMENTS, ASK THE ILLUSTRATOR
sections.content:
Q: Please tell us Sugamo Ryou's three sizes.

A: Unless I ask Hidari-sensei, I don't know either.

sections.heading: ANTHOLOGIES HE'D WANT TO WRITE FOR
sections.content:
Q: Among other authors' works, is there anything that makes you want to contribute to an official anthology?

A: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure and LIVE A LIVE. For JoJo, I'd want to write a sequel to Deadman's Q;[ref:deadmans-q-again] for LIVE A LIVE, I'd want to novelize every single chapter — especially the sci-fi chapter, which I'd love to take another crack at.[ref:live-a-live-again]

sections.heading: A COVER ILLUSTRATED BY DAD
sections.content:
Q: Among the characters in Iruma-sensei's works, I really love Kitsukawa Eiji — any chance of a story with him as the lead? Also, when will we get a book with a cover illustrated by Iruma's father?

A: There are already books that include illustrations by my father.[ref:father-illustrations] Incidentally, my father once said, half-joking, that he'd love to draw a cover someday.

sections.heading: IS LOVING BOOKS ENOUGH TO BECOME A WRITER?
sections.content:
Q: People often say that a hobby and a job are two different things. If that's true, does that mean it's not okay to become a writer just because you love books? Is writing books something that brings Iruma-sensei joy?

A: There are plenty of examples of people who love eating becoming chefs, so as far as motivation goes, that should be fine. That said, writing books isn't really all that fun in itself — it is a job, after all. If something sells well, or someone tells me it was interesting, that's when I actually feel happy.

references.title: Kotaro Isaka and Takehiko Inoue
references.note: Kotaro Isaka is a bestselling Japanese novelist known for works like Golden Slumber and Grasshopper. Takehiko Inoue is one of Japan's most celebrated manga artists, creator of Slam Dunk and Vagabond. Iruma's comparison casts himself as a total newcomer being asked to sit across from an industry giant.

references.title: "Atonose Sakusaku"
references.note: Iruma's phrasing riffs on "atonose sakusaku" ("add it after, keep it crispy"), the long-running advertising slogan for Nissin's Donbei instant udon and soba, which ships with a separate crispy tempura topping meant to be added just before eating so it doesn't go soggy.

references.title: The Origin of My Small-Scale Miracle
references.note: Volume 7 of Dengeki Bunko MAGAZINE (April 2009) came packaged with a collaborative short-story booklet titled "April, That Was—", which included Iruma's contribution, "April, That Was—A Lifespan. My Small-Scale Miracle." Iruma later wrote a story set twenty years after that short story, publishing it as the standalone novel My Small-Scale Miracle in October of the same year; a print (bunko) edition followed in May 2011 with an additional epilogue chapter.

references.title: The Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy Manga Adaptation
references.note: The manga adaptation of Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy concluded in July 2013 after three collected volumes.

references.title: Japanese Civil Law and Sibling Marriage
references.note: As a point of fact, Japanese civil law does not actually prohibit marriage between people who become siblings only through their parents' remarriage (as opposed to full or half-siblings by blood) — the questioner's premise here is a bit of an exaggeration for comic effect.

references.title: Ludman's Proposal Scene
references.note: A repeat reference to the marriage-proposal sequence in Dragon Quest V, where speaking to Ludman (Flora's father) at the wrong moment produces a comically rejecting response — the same joke used in Round 5 of this Q&A.

references.title: Flora, Bianca, and Their Children's Hair Color
references.note: In Dragon Quest V, whichever woman the hero marries determines his children's hair color: marrying Bianca results in blond(-ish, or "yellow") hair, while marrying Flora results in blue hair. Iruma's comment about preferring "blue over yellow" is a reference to this outcome, confirming his choice of Flora as the game's bride.

references.title: The Naked Idiot Comes Running
references.note: Baka ga Zenra de Yattekuru ("The Naked Idiot Comes Running") is a real MediaWorks Bunko novel by Iruma Hitoma, published in July 2012, following a struggling aspiring novelist whose life is upended by a naked stranger crashing his college welcome party. It later received a manga adaptation as well.

references.title: The Super Iruma War Short Stories
references.note: "Super Iruma War" was a set of six crossover short stories written to celebrate Iruma's fifth anniversary as an author, bringing characters from separate series (including Liar, Broken; Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy; The Lizard King; and "The Sky Falls Because of Eyes") into shared scenarios. The particular story referenced here, "Mixer, Side B," was published in Volume 27 of Dengeki Bunko MAGAZINE in August 2012.

references.title: "New World" (Theme Song)
references.note: "New World" is the theme song for Iruma's fifth-anniversary multimedia project Arata Naru Sekai ("A New World"), a combined manga/novel/anime release. Iruma wrote the lyrics; the song was composed and arranged by Satoru Kousaki (of the group MONACA) and performed by Marina Kawano (河野マリナ, whose name is also rendered 河野万里奈). It was included on Kawano's debut album, First Touch, released December 11, 2013.

references.title: Ayu and Mai
references.note: Iruma later did settle on names for Akkyun and Ma-chan's twin daughters: Ayu and Mai, formally introduced in Volume 11 of The Lying Boy and the Broken Girl (published 2017), a special release marking Iruma's tenth anniversary as a novelist. The names are recombinations of their parents' names, Ai and Mayu.

references.title: Healthya Green Tea
references.note: Healthya (ヘルシア緑茶) is a green tea brand produced by Kao, marketed in Japan for its fat-burning health claims. The questioner is referencing a scene from Iruma's short story "Season of Static."

references.title: "My and Ma-chan's Diary"
references.note: "My and Ma-chan's Diary" was originally serialized daily for one month in 2008 on a Dengeki Bunko e-book platform, later collected in the 2011 booklet "Mii-kun and Ma-chan's ×× Life." It comprises 31 entries, framed as Akkyun's diary running from January 1st to January 31st.

references.title: Deadman's Q
references.note: A repeat reference to Deadman's Q, Hirohiko Araki's short spin-off manga following Yoshikage Kira after the events of Diamond Is Unbreakable (Part 4) of JoJo's Bizarre Adventure.

references.title: LIVE A LIVE
references.note: A repeat reference to Square's 1994 RPG LIVE A LIVE, whose eight era-spanning chapters Iruma has previously said he'd like to novelize in full, having already written an official spin-off short story for its science-fiction chapter.

references.title: Iruma's Father's Illustrations
references.note: My Small-Scale Miracle includes an illustration of a pair of shoes drawn by Iruma's father, and his father's artwork has also appeared periodically in the author-bio sections of Iruma's other books.
